what_this_is: The Workshop row for the better-auth-official folder: official Better Auth (TypeScript) on node, set up as its docs show, signing people in and acting as the OAuth authorization server MCP clients such as Claude and ChatGPT connect through.

payload.label: Run the official Better Auth sign-in server (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Start official Better Auth: email and password, passkeys, two factor, email codes, magic links, API keys, JWTs, and the OAuth server MCP clients sign in through
payload.description: Starts official Better Auth (the TypeScript library, set up as https://www.better-auth.com/docs shows) on node with the built-in node:sqlite database. Plugins: email and password with password reset, passkey, two factor (TOTP and backup codes), email OTP, magic link, multi session, API keys, JWT (EdDSA, keys at {base_path}/jwks), MCP (the OAuth 2.1 authorization server for MCP clients, with Client ID Metadata Documents; discovery at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server and /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource) device authorization, and bearer (so a device's session token works as Authorization: Bearer, as the device docs require). MCP access tokens are EdDSA JWTs with header typ at+jwt, the JWKS kid, and aud naming settings.json mcp.resource (the MCP door's address). As the JWT docs require with MCP, settings.json disabled_paths turns off the session /token route by default; OAuth clients get tokens from {base_path}/oauth2/token. Port, base URL, issuer, audience, passkey relying party, trusted origins, MCP resource and pages, the SQLite file, the session cookie name (__Host-trillion_session) and where email goes are all in settings.json; the secret comes from BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and is never printed.

settings.description: Optional path to a settings file, put where {settings} is in the command. Leave it out to use tools/better-auth-official/settings.json.

output_schema.description: The server keeps running and answers on the port in settings.json. GET {base_url}{base_path}/ok answers {"ok":true} when it is ready.

invoke.run: cd trillion-workshop/tools/better-auth-official && BETTER_AUTH_SETTINGS={settings} npx auth migrate --config auth.mjs -y && BETTER_AUTH_SETTINGS={settings} node server.mjs
needs: node 22.13 or newer (node:sqlite without a flag)
BETTER_AUTH_SECRET in the environment: a random secret of at least 32 characters
invoke.say: This runs on any computer that serves an account, the person's own or a rented place: the same clone, npm ci and run work on each. Set BETTER_AUTH_SECRET from the vault by name (never print it), edit tools/better-auth-official/settings.json for the port, issuer, passkey origin, MCP resource, database file and email, then run `run`; the migrate step creates or updates the tables the Better Auth CLI generates (schema.sql). Check GET {base_url}{base_path}/ok. Email (password reset, codes, magic links) goes to settings.json email.command as JSON on stdin, or to the email.outbox file when no command is set.

provenance.source: better-auth 1.7.23 with @better-auth/passkey, @better-auth/api-key, @better-auth/mcp and @better-auth/cimd 1.7.23, configured from the docs pages for installation, the Node integration, the SQLite adapter (node:sqlite), email and password, and the passkey, two-factor, email-otp, magic-link, multi-session, api-key, jwt (OAuth Provider Mode), mcp, cimd device-authorization and bearer plugins; schema.sql from `auth generate`
